sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling from the selected law \(p=P(E,W,Z\mid S=1)\), with an independent margin multinomial sample in design A when margins are estimated and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes one draw of \((E,W,Z)\) conditional on \(S=1\); the finite SCM is a superpopulation model.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X\) is binary and may be confounded with the response type; in design B its assignment probability may depend on \((U,Z)\).
sampling_model.overlap: All population selected cells are positive. A nonempty supplied-margin fiber forces every population cell margin to be positive. Wald inference additionally requires separated incident charts, common first derivatives, smooth local continuations, and target covariance bounded away from singularity; Hausdorff equivalence of profile and Wald regions also requires a locally saturated compatible observable neighborhood.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Reduced selected-table and independent margin coordinates use empirical multinomial frequencies and the block-diagonal plug-in covariance. The deterministic chart selector uses the stated tolerance and full-square fallback. Transition inference profiles the exact multinomial discrepancy over the complete compatible target fiber and applies Berger--Boos calibration; this gives finite-sample coverage even when chart selection or point identification fails.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 identify PN and PS under positive observed tables, invertible proxy matrices, and unequal determinant-ratio conditions.
Formula (5) identifies a causal effect under a proxy rank condition without identifying the measurement mechanism.
Proposition 3.3 characterizes infinitesimal rigidity of an exact nonnegative factorization by its admissible-motion cone.
Theorems 5--9 give necessary support conditions and sufficient sequential recovery conditions for selected NMF factors.
Theorem 1 gives sufficient positive-scattering thresholds for minimality and uniqueness of nonnegative tensor decompositions.
Theorem 3.4 gives a regular root-n estimator for a linear proximal target without uniqueness of the bridge solution.

Theorem 1 identifies all four response-type probabilities in a randomized experiment under positive conditional tables, \(W\perp Z\mid U\), \(X\perp(U,Z,W)\), invertible cell matrices, and unequal determinant ratios; equations (8)--(11) give plug-in estimators.

Theorem 1 identifies all four joint probabilities of binary potential-outcome types under Figure 2(b)'s IV-plus-proxy recursive factorization, the five invertibility requirements in condition (i), the cross-treatment second-column separation in condition (ii), and the two exclusion restrictions in condition (iii).

Theorems 2--5 give sound closed-form bounds for a representative family of discrete probabilities of causation from standard experimental and observational distributions, while general-dimensional tightness remains open in the current version.
Conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without strong identification.
E-variable inversion yields exact anytime-valid confidence sets for contingency-table parameters.
Theorem 4 identifies PN and PS under exogeneity and monotonicity, and equations (15)--(18) give sharp bounds otherwise.

body.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, a boundary-complete structural atlas decides PN/PS target rigidity. It exhausts rank-two orientations and the four disjoint rank-one modes, retains equal-endpoint split vectors and inactive rows, and adds response-level residual forests for the unknown-margin relevant-IV design. A one-copy real-algebraic component evaluator returns an exact common target, two legal same-observable SCMs, or model incompatibility. Its fixed-alphabet termination contract now separates the explicit structural-template count from sequentially composed connected-component, projection, and exact-labeling bounds. Arbitrary real inputs are handled relative to coefficient-field arithmetic, order, sign, and root oracles; rational inputs have composed degree and height bounds. Exact confidence-fiber coverage remains universal, while Wald and Hausdorff equivalence are confined to separated, locally saturated rigid profiles.

project_justification.gap: Published regular proxy formulas do not classify PN/PS constancy when ranks fall, coefficients reach support faces, endpoints coincide, response rows become inactive, or shared-instrument equations couple unknown population margins. General real-algebraic decidability alone also does not expose the causal response-cycle obstruction.
project_justification.niche: The four response types form a labeled cycle whose causal target may be rigid even while nuisance factorizations vary. Exhaustive local edge modes, shared endpoints, and residual forests reduce every legal fiber to finitely many one-copy component problems without replacing the causal classification by a two-copy unequal-target predicate.
project_justification.fill: The completed compiler gives necessary and sufficient compatibility and target-agreement tests for both supplied-margin and relevant-IV designs. It computes connected components before target projection, tests a sampled component against a different target value, and returns exact algebraic values or legal full-SCM twins. Its termination theorem multiplies the explicit causal chart count by sequential component, projection, and labeling bounds, with a separately composed rational-height bound. The statistical layer combines separated-chart Wald inference with universal finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage.

body.related_work: Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026) provide the selected response-type model and regular PN/PS inversion formulas; the compatibility-qualified anchor theorem proves agreement on that regular domain and extends classification, not their formula, to singular and boundary fibers. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023) identify response-type probabilities in a randomized no-selection proxy experiment, and Kawakami (2021) identifies the corresponding IV-plus-proxy quantities under its stated invertibility and separation conditions. The atlas agrees on those overlaps and separately classifies an explicit selected boundary datum outside Kawakami's invertibility domain, without a subsumption claim. Nonnegative-factorization rigidity work supplies useful geometry but does not state causal target constancy on this labeled cycle. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006) supply the classical roadmap, connected-component, projection, sampling, sign, and real-root algorithms used after the causal L/R/E/D and residual-forest atlas is proved exhaustive; the complexity theorem composes their output formats in execution order rather than treating their bounds independently.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact compiler is a theorem-level symbolic procedure, not a claim of a completed production implementation or favorable variable-alphabet complexity. Its displayed complexity envelope is deliberately conservative and is obtained by sequentially composing published effective bounds after multiplying by the causal structural-template count. Over arbitrary real observables, computation is relative to effective arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles. A rational field expression is returned only when constructed; otherwise the exact output remains a real-univariate and Thom encoding. Strictly positive twins are guaranteed only when both chosen cycle witnesses are on interior support charts. Universal confidence coverage does not imply shrinking at a nonidentified transition, and first-order Hausdorff agreement requires a locally saturated separated rigid profile. The frozen materials still lack the released numerical GEUVADIS count table and binarization thresholds, so no empirical compatibility or rigidity verdict for that dataset is claimed here.
body.honest_scope: The mathematical contribution is the exhaustive fixed-alphabet structural response-cycle classifier plus exact one-copy component evaluation. Empty fibers are reported as incompatibility and are non-rigid under the cardinality-one definition. The termination result gives an explicit structural count and a sequential composition of published component, projection, labeling, degree, and rational-height bounds; it does not claim favorable growing-alphabet complexity. The field-relative and rational-input output tiers are distinct. Regular overlap results are agreement checks, and the Kawakami boundary example is a one-law scope separation only. Wald inference requires chart separation, common first derivatives, smooth continuations, proportional margin sampling when applicable, and nonsingular target covariance. Exact confidence-fiber coverage holds without those conditions; its optional Wald-equivalence clause additionally requires a locally saturated compatible neighborhood. The GEUVADIS application remains an audit protocol conditional on the graph and on recovery of the actual released table, not a new numerical reanalysis.
